nodes.name: Theorem 1.4, Theorem 1.5
Proposition 4.6, Proposition 10.5
nodes.statement:
Consider the Best-of-three on an $f^{\mathrm{Bo3}}$-good $G(2n,p,q)$ such that $p$ and $q$ are constants.

If $q/p>1/7$ and $|\delta_2^{(0)}|=o(1)$, then it holds w.h.p.~that $|\delta_2^{(\tau)}|>\kappa$ for some $\tau=O(\log n)$ and some constant $\kappa>0$.

Let $p,q$ are constants and consider the Best-of-two on $G(2n,p,q)$ that is both $f^{\mathrm{Bo2}}_1$-good and $f^{\mathrm{Bo2}}_2$-good.
If $q/p>\sqrt{5}-2$ and $|\delta_2^{(0)}|=o(1)$, then it holds w.h.p.~that $|\delta_2^{(\tau)}|>\epsilon$ for some $\tau=O(\log n)$ and some constant $\epsilon>0$.

nodes.name: Proposition 4.4, Proposition 10.3
nodes.statement:
Consider the Best-of-three on an $f^{\mathrm{Bo3}}$-good $G(2n,p,q)$ such that $r=q/p<1/7$ is a constant.
Then there exists a positive constant $\epsilon=\epsilon(r)$ satisfying
\begin{align*}
\mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[\langle {\boldsymbol \delta'} \rangle_+\not\in B(\mathbf{d}_2^*,\epsilon) \,\middle|\, \langle {\boldsymbol \delta} \rangle_+\in B(\mathbf{d}_2^*,\epsilon)\right] \leq \exp(-\Omega(n)).
\end{align*}

In particular, 


$T_{\mathrm{cons}}(A) = \exp(\Omega(n))$ w.h.p.~for any $A$ satisfying $\langle {\boldsymbol \delta} \rangle_+ \in B(\mathbf{d}_2^*,\epsilon)$.

Consider the Best-of-two on $G(2n,p,q)$ that is both $f^{\mathrm{Bo2}}_1$-good and $f^{\mathrm{Bo2}}_2$-good.
Suppose that $r=q/p<\sqrt{5}-2$ is a constant.
Then, there exists a positive constant $\epsilon=\epsilon(r)$ satisfying
\begin{align*}
\mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[{\boldsymbol \delta'}\not\in B(\mathbf{d}_2^*,\epsilon) \,\middle|\, {\boldsymbol \delta}\in B(\mathbf{d}_2^*,\epsilon)\right] \leq \exp(-\Omega(n)).
\end{align*}

In particular, 


$T_{\mathrm{cons}}(A) = \exp(\Omega(n))$ holds w.h.p.~for any $A\subseteq V$ satisfying $\langle {\boldsymbol \delta} \rangle_+ \in B(\mathbf{d}_2^*,\epsilon)$.

nodes.name: Proposition 4.5, Proposition 10.4
nodes.statement:
Consider the Best-of-three on an $f^{\mathrm{Bo3}}$-good $G(2n,p,q)$ such that $r=q/p$ is a constant.
Then, there exists a universal constant $\epsilon=\epsilon(r)>0$ satisfying the following: $T_{\mathrm{cons}}(A) \leq O(\log\log n+\log n/\log (np))$ holds w.h.p.~for all $A\subseteq V$ with $\min\{|A|,2n-|A|\}\leq \epsilon n$.

Consider the Best-of-two on $G(2n,p,q)$ that is both $f^{\mathrm{Bo2}}_1$-good and $f^{\mathrm{Bo2}}_2$-good.
Suppose that $r=q/p$ is a constant.
Then, there exists a universal constant $\epsilon=\epsilon(r)>0$ satisfying the following:
$T_{\mathrm{cons}}(A)\leq O(\log\log n+\log n/\log (np))$ holds w.h.p.~for all $A\subseteq V$ with $\min\{|A|,2n-|A|\}\leq \epsilon n$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.2, Theorem 1.3
Proposition 4.3, Proposition 10.2
nodes.statement:
For any sequence $(\mathbf{d}^{(t)})_{t=0}^\infty$, $\lim_{t\to\infty} \langle \mathbf{d}^{(t)} \rangle_+=\mathbf{d}^*_i$ for some $i\in\{1,2,3,4\}$.
In addition, if $u<\frac{3}{4}$ and a positive constant $\kappa>0$ exists such that the initial point $\mathbf{d}^{(0)}=(d^{(0)}_1,d^{(0)}_2)\in S$ satisfies $|d^{(0)}_2|>\kappa$, then $\lim_{t\to\infty} \langle \mathbf{d}^{(t)} \rangle_+ =\mathbf{d}^*_4$.

For any sequence $(\mathbf{d}^{(t)})_{t=0}^\infty$, $\lim_{t\to\infty} \langle \mathbf{d}^{(t)} \rangle_+=\mathbf{d}^*_i$ for some $i\in\{1,2,3,4\}$.
Furthermore, if $u<\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2}$ and a positive constant $\kappa>0$ exists such that the initial point $\mathbf{d}^{(0)}=(d^{(0)}_1,d^{(0)}_2)\in S$ satisfies $|d^{(0)}_2|>\kappa$, then $\lim_{t\to\infty}\langle \mathbf{d}^{(t)} \rangle_+=\mathbf{d}^*_4$.

nodes.name: Proposition 7.8
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathbf{a}^*$ be a fixed point satisfying either 7.6~or~7.7.
Then, there exist $\tau=O(\log n)$ and a constant $\epsilon'>0$ such that the followings hold w.h.p.:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item $\|\beta^{(\tau)}\|_\infty > \epsilon'$, and
\item $|\beta^{(\tau)}_j| \leq \epsilon'$ for any $j\in [2]$ of $|\lambda_j|\leq 1$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Proposition 7.2
Proposition 7.3
Theorem 3.2, Theorem 6.2
nodes.statement:
Suppose that $f:[0,1]\to [0,1]$ is a polynomial function with constant degree, $p=\omega(\log n/n)$ and $q\geq \log n/n^2$. 
Then $G(2n,p,q)$ is $f$-good w.h.p.

Let $f_1$ and $f_2$ be polynomials with constant degree.
Consider an $(f_1,f_2)$-polynomial voting process, on an $f_1$-good and $f_2$-good $G(2n,p,q)$ starting with vertex set $A^{(0)}\subseteq V$ of opinion $1$.
Let $(A^{(t)})_{t=0}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of random vertex subsets defined by $A^{(t+1)}\mathrel{\mathop:}= (A^{(t)})'$ for each $t\geq 0$.
Let $({\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(t)})_{t=0}^{\infty}$, where ${\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(t)}=(\alpha^{(t)}_1,\alpha^{(t)}_2)$ and $\alpha^{(t)}_i=|A^{(t)}\cap V_i|/n$.
Define a mapping $H=(H_1,H_2)$ as
\begin{align*}
H_i(a_1,a_2)=a_i f_1\left(\frac{a_i+ra_{3-i}}{1+r}\right)
+
(1-a_i) f_2\left(\frac{a_i+ra_{3-i}}{1+r}\right) \,\,\,\text{for $i=1,2$}.
\end{align*}

Define $(\mathbf{a}^{(t)})_{t=0}^\infty$ as $\mathbf{a}^{(0)}={\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(0)}$ and $\mathbf{a}^{(t+1)}=H(\mathbf{a}^{(t)})$ for each $t\geq 0$. 
Then, 
there exists a constant $C>0$ such that
\begin{align*}
\forall 0\leq t\leq n^{o(1)},\forall A^{(0)}\subseteq V\,:\,\mathop{\mathbf{Pr}}\left[\|{\boldsymbol \alpha}^{(t)}-\mathbf{a}^{(t)}\|_\infty \leq C^t \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{np}}+\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}\right)\right] \geq 1-n^{-\Omega(1)}.
\end{align*}

nodes.name: Lemma 8.1, Lemma 8.3, Lemma 8.4, Lemma 8.2, Lemma 8.5, Lemma 8.6
nodes.statement:
For a vertex set $V$ with $|V|=N$, let $(I_e)_{e\in \binom{V}{2}}$ be $\binom{N}{2}$ independent binary random variables. 
Let $p \mathrel{\mathop:}= \max_{e\in \binom{V}{2}}\mathbf{E}[I_e]$.
Suppose that $N p \geq 1$.
For $\ell+1$ vertex subsets $S_0, S_1, \ldots, S_\ell$, let
\begin{align*}
W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)&\mathrel{\mathop:}=\sum_{s\in S_0}\prod_{i\in[\ell]}\deg_{S_i}(s), 
\\
\hat{W}(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)&\mathrel{\mathop:}= \sum_{s\in S_0}\prod_{i\in[\ell]}\mathbf{E}[\deg_{S_i}(s)]
\end{align*}
where $\deg_S(v)=\sum_{s\in S\setminus \{v\}}I_{\{v,s\}}$ for $S\subseteq V$ and $v\in V$.

Then two positive constants $C_1, C_2$ exist such that the following holds with probability $1-N^{-C_1}$: 
\begin{align*}
\forall S_0, S_1, \ldots, S_\ell: \bigl|W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)-\hat{W}(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)\bigr| 
\leq C_2N (N p)^{\ell-1/2}.
\end{align*}

Suppose the same setting of 8.1.

Then two positive constants $C_1, C_2$ exist such that the following holds with probability $1-N^{-C_1}$: 
\begin{align*}
\forall S_0, S_1, \ldots, S_\ell: 
\bigl|W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)-\mathbf{E}[W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)]\bigr|\leq  C_2 N(N p)^{\ell-1/2}.

\end{align*}

Suppose the same setting of 8.1.
Then for any vertex subsets $S_0, S_1, \ldots, S_\ell$ 
and for any $i_*\in \{0\}\cup [\ell]$, 
a positive constant $C$ exists such that
\begin{align*}
\left|\mathbf{E}[W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)]-\hat{W}(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_\ell)\right|
\leq 

C|S_{i_*}|(N p)^{\ell-1}.
\end{align*}

Let $V$ be a set of $|V|=N$ vertices
and fix $l+1$ subsets $S_0, S_1, \ldots, S_l\subseteq V$. 
For any $\mathbf{s}=(s_0,s_1,\ldots, s_l)\in S_0\times S_1\times \cdots \times S_l$, 
define 
\begin{align*}
U(\mathbf{s})&\mathrel{\mathop:}= \{s_i: i\in \{0\}\cup [l]\}.
\end{align*}
Consider $\sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathcal{S}}}p^{|\mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s})|}$, where 
$p\in [1/N,1]$, $\mathcal{S}\subseteq S_0\times S_1\times \cdots \times S_l$ and  
\begin{align*}
\mathcal{F}: S_0\times S_1\times \cdots \times S_l \to 2^{\binom{V}{2}}.
\end{align*}
Suppose that the following three conditions hold for any $\mathbf{s}\in \mathcal{S}$:  
(1) $|\mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s})|\leq k$, 
(2) $\mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s})\subseteq \binom{U(\mathbf{s})}{2}$ 
and 
(3) the graph $G(\mathbf{s})=\bigl(U(\mathbf{s}), \mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s})\bigr)$ is connected.
Let $L\subseteq \{0\}\cup [l]$ be the set of indices such that $S_i\cap S_j=\emptyset$ for any $i,j\in L$ $(i\neq j)$.
Then
\begin{align*}
\sum_{\substack{\mathbf{s}\in \mathcal{S}}}p^{|\mathcal{F}(\mathbf{s})|}\leq \mathcal{B}_{l+1}N (N p)^k\frac{\prod_{i\in L}|S_i|}{N ^{|L|}}
\end{align*}
where $\mathcal{B}_l$ denotes the $l$-th Bell number.

Suppose that $0\leq q\leq p=\omega(\log n/n)$.
Then two positive constants $C_1, C_2$ exist such that $G(2n,p,q)$ satisfies the following with probability $1-O(n^{-C_1})$:
\begin{align*}
\forall v\in V: |\deg(v)-n(p+q)|\leq C_2\sqrt{np\log n}.
\end{align*}

Suppose that $0\leq q\leq p=\omega(\log n/n)$.
Let $\mathcal{S}(A)=\bigl\{ S\cap U: S\in \{A,V\setminus A, V\}, U\in \{V_1, V_2, V\} \bigr\}$ for $A\subseteq V$.
For any constant $\ell$, two positive constants $C_1, C_2$ exist such that $G(2n,p,q)$ satisfies the following with probability $1-O(n^{-C_1})$:
\begin{align*}
\lefteqn{\forall A\subseteq V, \forall S_0, \ldots, S_{\ell-1}\in \mathcal{S}(A):}\\

&\bigl|W(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell-1}, A)-\hat{W}(S_0;S_1,\ldots,S_{\ell-1}, A)\bigr|\leq  C_2 |A|\sqrt{\log n}(np)^{\ell-1/2}.
\end{align*}
